evidence.claim: Shinko's IR FAQ states that the tender offer period ran from February 18, 2025 to March 18, 2025, the tender offer was successfully completed, and the company's shares were delisted on June 6, 2025; it also states the shares cannot be traded on the Prime Market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
evidence.source_title: FAQs | Investor Relations | SHINKO ELECTRIC INDUSTRIES CO., LTD.

evidence.claim: Shinko's FY2024 financial-results material listed the corporate-action schedule: last trading day June 5, 2025, delisting date June 6, 2025, and share-consolidation effective date June 10, 2025.

Shinko's February 2025 tender-offer announcement stated that its shares were listed on the TSE Prime Market at that time, but could be delisted through prescribed procedures depending on the tender-offer result and squeeze-out procedures.
evidence.source_title: Announcement Regarding Commencement of the Tender Offer for the Shares of SHINKO ELECTRIC INDUSTRIES CO., LTD. by JICC-04, Ltd.

evidence.claim: Shinko's semiconductor-package product page lists substrate products including flip-chip package substrates, PBGA substrates, 2.3D package substrates, and substrate with optical wiring, plus IC assembly products including optical chiplet/CPO.
evidence.source_title: Semiconductor Package | Products | SHINKO ELECTRIC INDUSTRIES CO., LTD.

evidence.claim: Shinko's flip-chip package substrate page says demand for flip-chip package substrates using a build-up process has increased with performance improvement of IC chips in PCs and servers, and lists high-end servers, GPU, CPU/MPU, ASIC, and FPGA as applications.
evidence.source_title: Flip-Chip Package Substrate ~DLL/DLL3~ | Services | SHINKO ELECTRIC INDUSTRIES CO., LTD.

evidence.claim: Shinko's business page describes flip-chip type packages, also called build-up substrates or flip-chip packages, as mainly used in advanced IC chips such as CPUs for computers and servers, and says the company aims to support markets related to IoT and AI.
evidence.source_title: Our Business | About SHINKO | SHINKO ELECTRIC INDUSTRIES CO., LTD.

evidence.claim: Shinko's individual-investor product explainer states that for data-center servers, its flip-chip package substrates are used in server CPUs and its heat spreaders disperse heat generated from CPUs.
evidence.source_title: Our Products: With You Every Day | To Understand SHINKO | About SHINKO

evidence.claim: Shinko's lidded flip-chip package page describes high-heat-dissipation flip-chip packaging, various flip-chip bonding technologies for high-density IC chips, and applications including processors for servers and LSI packages requiring high heat dissipation.
evidence.source_title: Lidded Flip-Chip Package | Services | SHINKO ELECTRIC INDUSTRIES CO., LTD.

memory_update.text: 6967.T / Shinko Electric Industries maps strongly to AI/HPC package substrates and advanced semiconductor packaging as a private/reference node, not as an active public-market candidate.

Shinko's product evidence supports relevance to flip-chip package substrates, server CPU substrates, GPU/CPU/MPU/ASIC/FPGA applications, heat spreaders, IC assembly, and optical chiplet/CPO packaging.

Shinko should be removed or deprioritized from tradable candidate lists because its shares were delisted from the TSE Prime Market on June 6, 2025 after the JICC-04 tender offer and share-consolidation process.

Need replacement public-market mappings for the same substrate chokepoint: still-listed substrate makers, ABF-film suppliers, copper surface-treatment chemistry suppliers, plating/laser-drilling equipment suppliers, inspection/test vendors, and thermal-management component suppliers.

Need customer-specific and financial-materiality evidence for AI accelerator exposure in adjacent names: revenue mix, utilization, backlog, capacity additions, qualification status, customer concentration, and whether AI/HPC substrate tightness is already priced.

summary: Shinko Electric Industries was a valid reference-leader mapping for the AI/HPC advanced-packaging substrate node, but it should be downgraded as a public-market candidate because its common shares were delisted from the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime Market on June 6, 2025 after the JICC-04 tender offer and squeeze-out process. The operating company remains relevant as a private supply-chain reference for flip-chip package substrates, high-end server/CPU/GPU/ASIC/FPGA packaging, heat spreaders, and related advanced packaging know-how. For the Serenity funnel, 6967.T should be retained as a reference relationship, not as a tradable underfollowed candidate. Next mapping should look laterally at still-listed substrate competitors, material/chemistry suppliers, inspection/test suppliers, or equipment/tooling nodes that sell into the same AI/HPC package substrate bottleneck.
